Sam (Acme): Hi team — our March invoice (inv_2026_03_17) is $275.12 but the usage dashboard totals $249.89. That's a $25.23 gap, same currency (USD). Can someone explain why invoice != dashboard?
Maya (Support Lead): Sorry about that, Sam. Can you paste the invoice snippet + a screenshot of the dashboard totals? Do you have the account id so we can pull raw meter events? :raising_hand:
Sam (Acme): Account: acct_9fX. Invoice lines pasted below: 
```
- generation: 2,345,678 tokens => $231.45
- embeddings: 12,345 units => $18.10
- tax/adjustments => $25.57
Total => $275.12
```
Dashboard (billing -> usage) shows: total usage charges $249.89 (no adjustments). Invoice currency USD. No multi-currency conversion.
Nora - Billing: Thanks, Sam. Can you confirm whether you saw many tiny requests around month end? We recently found an edge where per-request rounding to cents can accumulate. Also need the invoice id (you gave it) — we are pulling the line-item breakdown now.
billing-bot: Automatic note: invoice inv_2026_03_17 linked to acct_9fX. Bill run completed 2026-03-17T03:41Z. Aggregation job: monthly_rollup_v2.
Eli (Infra Eng): Quick theory: our meter stores costs in microcents (integer) but historically we applied rounding at the request granularity when producing line-items, then summed. Dashboard shows raw microcents aggregated and then rounded at the display/invoice level in a different place. Those two rounding points can diverge if many small events exist. Do you have any health-check or token-minimizing traffic?
Sam (Acme): Yes — we have a short-lived health ping that calls the API and consumes 1-2 tokens ~50k times a month (was intended to be local but jumped to prod after a deploy). Could that cause the diff?
Eli (Infra Eng): Exactly. Example math: price_per_token = $0.00002 (2e-5). For a request consuming 1 token raw_cost = $0.00002 => rounded to $0.00 if we round to cents per request. But we actually round to nearest cent per request in legacy billing (so many sub-cent requests become $0.00 or $0.01 depending on rounding algorithm), producing non-linear accumulation. Contrast: invoice-level calculation sums raw microcents then divides by 100 and rounds once. That yields a different total.
Eli (Infra Eng): Quick calc example (simplified):
```
- 50,000 health requests * 1 token * $0.00002 = $1.00 raw
- If per-request rounding sends 50k * rounded($0.00002) => 50k * $0.00 = $0.00 (if floor) OR 50k * $0.01 = $500 (if ceil) depending on rule -> big variance.
```
Maya (Support Lead): That example is extreme bc rounding per request to cents isn't logical for micro-unit pricing. We need to know exactly where the rounding happened for this invoice. Nora, can billing confirm whether the line item generator applied rounding per-event or per-aggregate for this customer in this run?
Nora - Billing: Looking at the run logs for monthly_rollup_v2: invoice generator applied rounding per-charge for legacy accounts (we started migrating accounts to invoice-level rounding in 2026-02). acct_9fX is still on legacy per-request rounding. I can see a line in the run logs: `charge_rounding_mode: per_event` for acct_9fX. That explains the delta.
Sam (Acme): So the dashboard uses raw aggregated microcents and the invoice used per-event rounded cents? That seems backwards — we were expecting invoice to match dashboard.
Eli (Infra Eng): Dashboard is computed from usage_events table and shows sum(raw_microcents)/100 with single final rounding. Legacy invoice code applied rounding per usage_event when creating line items. With lots of sub-cent events (health checks), rounding losses/gains sum to ~ $25 for your volume — matches the discrepancy.
Maya (Support Lead): Proposed remediation: 1) Apply a one-time credit of $25.23 to the customer to reconcile. 2) Offer to migrate acct_9fX to invoice-level rounding to avoid recurrence. 3) Create a fix: enforce invoice-level rounding by default and convert legacy accounts.
Nora - Billing: Agreed — creating a credit memo now. Credit amount: $25.23. Credit id: cr_2026_03_17_891. Will reflect on next billing cycle, can apply immediately if Sam wants.
Sam (Acme): Appreciate it. Immediate apply would be great, our finance team wants to close month. Thank you.
Eli (Infra Eng): I'll open an internal bug and link telemetry to prove root cause and migration steps. Repro steps for engineering:
```
1) Pull usage_events for acct_9fX for date range.
2) Compute per-event charge: round(cents(event_microcents/100)) and sum.
3) Compare to sum(event_microcents)/100 then round once.
4) Diff should match invoice - dashboard.
SQL (example):
SELECT SUM(ROUND(event_microcents/100.0,2)) AS per_event_sum, ROUND(SUM(event_microcents)/100.0,2) AS aggregate_sum FROM usage_events WHERE account_id='acct_9fX' AND ts >= '2026-03-01' AND ts < '2026-04-01';
```
Eli (Infra Eng): I'll attach the run logs and mark bug BI-5432 P2. Nora, can you confirm migration window and whether this affects other legacy accounts?
Nora - Billing: Running a query for accounts with `charge_rounding_mode: per_event` — ~312 accounts remain. We'll prioritize those with >$10 discrepancy risk. Will add acct_9fX to immediate migrate list.
Maya (Support Lead): Sam — we've created support ticket SUP-8976 and billing credit cr_2026_03_17_891 applied. Expect show back in ~30 minutes if you choose immediate apply. Also ticket BI-5432 tracks platform fix.
Sam (Acme): Thanks everyone. Please also add a short note to docs explaining rounding semantics so finance teams aren't surprised. :thumbsup:
